properties.title: Clin-JEPA: A Multi-Phase Co-Training Framework for Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining on EHR Patient Trajectories
properties.membership_basis: Reported implementation and evaluation of persistent clinical latent history advanced by a learned hourly transition; not merely a representation probe.
properties.bibliographic_review: Supplied title-page text and earlier page-image review notes; no external verification.

properties.hash_basis: SHA-256 recomputed from the packet PDF during local review; it matches the B010 assignment.
properties.review_provenance: The local PDF binary was accessible for SHA-256 verification. Page rendering was not performed in this synthesis. Inherited automated page-review records declare text and image review for all 42 physical pages; the alternate text-cache extraction is not cryptographically bound to the packet PDF.

properties.design: Retrospective single-system development and patient-held-out internal evaluation
properties.dependence: All axes reuse the same dataset and fitted models; not independent clinical replications.

properties.name: MIMIC-IV ICU
properties.sources: Raw tables and official mimic-code derived concepts
properties.access_terms: Not established by the supplied paper; dataset-family knowledge is not substituted.

properties.eligibility: Age ≥18; first ICU stay of hospital admission; duration ≥6 hours; at least one charted vital sign.
properties.split: Patient-level 70/15/15; all stays of a patient remain together.
properties.windowing: Stay truncation 336 hours; windows ≤72 hours; stride 12 hours for longer stays.
properties.count_boundary: Training-window count is not a training-patient count.

properties.selection: Windows longer than 24 hours; each horizon uses available observed targets.
properties.dependence: Overlapping windows; bootstrap clusters ICU stays, whereas Wilcoxon tests are described over windows.

properties.eligibility: Admission-anchored test stays with observed SOFA at every hour 0–71.
properties.definitions: Deteriorating: ΔSOFA≥3. Stable: not deteriorating, SOFA population SD≤1 and range≤2.
properties.boundary: Observed-state association, not admission-time forecast validation.

properties.hourly_eligibility: At least 24 hours of context and defined task label.
properties.comparator_coverage: CLMBR-T-base covers a strict subset; exact covered count not reported.
properties.boundary: Treatment-response labels include care decisions, not identified treatment effects.

properties.purpose: Research on hourly latent clinical pretraining, factual conditional forecasting and predictive representations.
properties.actual_action_authority: No clinical action selection or execution in reported experiments.

properties.name: CLIN-JEPA
properties.configuration: Final model reported in arXiv v5; optimizer step 11,776
properties.encoder: Qwen3-8B, 8.2B base parameters frozen; approximately 15.3M LoRA parameters; 4096-dimensional last-token embeddings.
properties.predictor: 92.5M parameters; six-layer block-causal Transformer; hidden 1024; eight attention heads.
properties.feedback: Native two-step training in warmup/finalization; observed online embeddings during co-training/alignment. Recursive state feedback at evaluation.
properties.identity_status: Source-supported implemented healthcare world model; no code execution or independent replication.

properties.name: V-JEPA 2-AC style
properties.scope: This paper's EHR comparator, not the original robotics system.
properties.training: Random-mask JEPA refinement; mask ratio 0.4; encoder guard fires at step 2250; separate predictor trained 20 epochs/15,400 steps.
properties.qualification: Guard crossing largely reflects scale contraction; Appendix C does not classify this encoder as collapsed under scale-free diagnostics.

properties.name: SFT baseline w/o JEPA
properties.configuration: Shared SFT encoder without JEPA refinement, plus separately trained latent predictor.
properties.boundary: Not just an SFT encoder; the evaluated system contains learned dynamics.

properties.name: CLIN-JEPA w/ separately trained predictor
properties.configuration: Final main-model encoder reused frozen; fresh predictor trained 20 epochs/15,400 steps.
properties.dependence: Shares the main encoder; zero encoder updates in this run exclude prior encoder construction.

properties.name: CLIN-JEPA w/o warmup
properties.evaluated_checkpoint: 2048, immediately after hard sync, before finalization
properties.boundary: Not budget- or final-checkpoint-matched to the main run.

properties.name: CLIN-JEPA w/o alignment
properties.boundary: Does not separately isolate alignment and synchronization.

properties.flow: Hourly clinical text → shared LLM encoder → ordered latent history → action-conditioned Transformer → recursive latent forecasts → optional pooled-feature supervised probes.
properties.future_feature_boundary: Uses recorded future care and actual record-end-dependent stopping/zero padding.

properties.boundary: One textual modality; heterogeneous clinical channels do not establish separate modality encoders.

properties.feedback: Predicted states after observed prefix; no measured-state correction within forecasts.

properties.scope: Post-SFT JEPA curriculum, excluding next-token initialization and supervised probes
properties.objective: L1 teacher-forced next-state plus two-step latent prediction
properties.controls: Predictor warmup, stop-gradient EMA target, temporal-variance monitoring, alignment and hard sync.
properties.boundary: Training stability controls are not clinical runtime safeguards.

properties.training: Supervised shallow MLP probes on frozen representations
properties.boundary: No causal-effect, reward, value or action-policy subrole.

properties.initialization: 24 observed hourly states/actions in rollout evaluation
properties.update: Predicted absolute next-state embedding appended/reused recursively

properties.representation: Structured clinical text encoded separately from state text
properties.mixed_semantics: Also contains measured device/response fields; not every field is an executable action.
properties.timing: Hourly sequence; multihour prescription orders written only at first hour.
properties.evaluation: Recorded care only; hypothetical alternatives not evaluated.
properties.inventory_boundary: procedureevents and invasive_line excluded from final input text.

properties.target: Same encoder's embedding of observed future state
properties.MASE: Ratio of mean model L1 error to mean copy-forward L1 error

properties.inputs: Observed state embeddings, not generated futures
properties.uncertainty: 1000 within-cohort stay bootstrap resamples; centroids/neighbors fixed for accuracy intervals.
properties.boundary: SOFA association, not intervention validity or prospective classifier validation.

properties.configuration: Frozen history-only representation and supervised probes

properties.rollout: 8/24/48 hours by hourly task; 48 hours for stay-level tasks
properties.information_boundary: Recorded post-context actions and actual record-end-dependent padding; not demonstrated as an origin-information-only forecast.

evidence_fragments.content:
Preprint.
arXiv:2605.10840v5  [cs.LG]  16 Sep 2026

Each of the three text inputs (state st, action at, and demographics d) is independently mapped to
a 4096-dimensional latent embedding by our encoder E: a Qwen3-8B language model whose base
weights are frozen and adapted via lightweight LoRA adapters. The same shared encoder processes
state, action, and demographics text via independent forward passes, with the last-token hidden state
taken as the embedding:

Within each hour we preserve every individual reading in its original
temporal order—including repeated measurements of the same variable (e.g., MAP sampled multiple
times during resuscitation)—as a lossless serialization that the encoder’s self-attention parses for
intra-hour dynamics; the latent trajectory predictor (§3.2) then composes these per-hour embeddings
into inter-hour dynamics. This representation requires no value imputation, no normalization, and no
modality-specific featurization: missing readings are simply absent from the state text, and numeric
values appear in their natural clinical units.

At inference, Pθ is retained and rolls out autoregressively: each predicted ˆzt+h is fed back as the state
input for step t+h+1 , yielding the simulated trajectory {ˆzt+h }Hh=1 used for downstream clinical tasks(Eq. 3). Unlike token-LM autoregression, which samples a discrete token and feeds the sample back,
our rollout feeds back the predicted continuous embedding directly—a deterministic conditional-
mean composition that lets a single predictor cover all forecast horizons h=1, . . . ,Hwith one shared
model rather than trainingHhorizon-specific predictors.

The rollout loss admits two regimes depending on whether the online and target encoders agree.
Native rollout(used when online ≡ target) chains the predictor’s own output back as the next-step state
input, mirroring inference behaviour.Teacher-forced rollout(used in phases where online ̸= target)
instead substitutes the real online embedding at each rollout step; this prevents a space-mismatch
failure where chained predictor outputs (trained to land in target space) would be fed back into a
pipeline that expects online-space inputs.

Datasets.All experiments use MIMIC-IV ICU [ 31], with 84,497 stays from 64,874 unique patients.
We split at thepatientlevel (70/15/15 train/val/test): all ICU stays from a given patient are assigned to
the same split, preventing patient-level data leakage between train, validation, and test. Per-hour state
and action representations are constructed from MIMIC-IV’s raw tables and the officialmimic-code
derived concept tables; the complete list of source tables and observation/action features is provided in
Appendix A. Each stay is windowed at 1-hour resolution following §3.1 (Tmax=72); stays exceeding
72 hours yield overlapping windows at stride 12 hours, totaling∼197K training windows.
Pretraining.CLIN-JEPA pretraining follows the five-phase curriculum of §4 (predictor warmup,
co-training, alignment, hard sync, finalize), executed on 8 × NVIDIA H200 GPUs for ∼54 wall-
clock hours (≈430 GPU-hours). Full optimizer and architecture hyperparameters are deferred to
Appendix B.

Inclusion criteria.An ICU stay enters the cohort if the patient is at least 18 years old at admission,
the stay is the first ICU stay of its hospital admission, it lasts at least 6 hours, and at least one vital
sign is charted during it. Stays are truncated at 336 hours (14 days). Trajectory windows are capped
at Tmax=72 hours (1-hour discretization); stays exceeding 72 hours yield overlapping windows at
stride 12 hours.

Excluded from the text inputs.The tables are the extraction inventory. The following extracted
fields do not enter the encoder’s text:
• Blood-gas rows from venous, capillary and mixed specimens; only arterial specimens are
kept, so that oxygenation values are comparable.
• Admission-level ICD diagnoses, which MIMIC-IV assigns at discharge: read at hour 0 they
would tell the encoder how the stay ended. The Charlson comorbidity index is derived from
the same codes and is excluded for the same reason.

Two further conventions apply. A prescription order that spans several hours is expanded by the
hourly discretization into one row per hour; the text writes it once, at its first hour. The demographics
textdis built from the cohort table as “Age: 53 years. Gender: Male. Race: White.”

Rollout protocol and per-horizon values.For every test window longer than C=24 hours (39,127
of 41,698) we encode the first C hours, roll the predictor out over the remaining hours (at most 48)
under the inference regime (each predicted state fed back as the next state input, with the true action
embeddings and demographics), and compare ˆzC+h withz C+h, the encoder’s embedding of the state
actually observed at hour C+h. A window of length L contributes to horizons h≤L−C (39,127
windows at h=1; 33,144 at h=48); every mean is taken over the windows valid at that horizon. ℓ1(h)
is the mean of ∥ˆzC+h −z C+h∥1, ℓcf1 (h) the mean of ∥zC −z C+h∥1, and MASE(h) =ℓ1(h)/ℓcf1 (h) is theratio of these two means (not the mean of per-window ratios). The one-hour relative step quoted in
§5.2 is ℓcf1 (1) divided by the mean ∥z∥1 of the same encoder’s test-set embeddings. State displacementis a property of the encoder and of the state text it reads: because every state text carries its hour index
(§3.1), displacement reflects the encoder’s representation of elapsed time as well as of physiological
change. Confidence intervals are stay-clustered bootstraps: 2,000 resamples of ICU stays, each drawn
with all of its windows, with the same resamples used for all four curves of a model so that their
intervals are mutually consistent. All numbers are computed by a single pipeline that asserts the
pairing of every prediction with its target window; the pipeline is part of the code release.

The top-64 subspace overlap is the mean squared cosine
of the principal angles between the 64 leading principal directions of the predicted and of the true
embeddings

Shared setup.The six models compared in §5.2 (Figure 2, Table 2) share an identical SFT-initialized
encoder (§3.1), an identical 92M-parameter predictor architecture (§3.2), and an identical held-out
evaluation split and rollout protocol (Appendix D). They differ in three respects only: the objective
under which the encoder is refined, if at all; whether the predictor is co-trained with the encoder or
trained separately on the frozen encoder’s cached embeddings; and the training budget and stopping
rule of each run. Because the runs therefore terminate at different training steps, Table 7 makes the
protocol of every model explicit; the encoder side and the predictor side are described in turn below.

Both failure modes are early,
monotone, and irreversible.

Under those diagnostics
only w/o warmup is collapsed; V-JEPA 2-AC style retains an effective rank close to the SFT encoder’s,
its threshold crossing reflecting a contraction of embedding scale (its mean ∥z∥1 is 16× smaller than
the SFT encoder’s) more than a loss of directions.

This appendix defines the cohorts, the distance normalization, and every statistic of §5.3, and reports
the robustness checks behind its last paragraph. All statistics are computed on the encoder’s per-hour
stateembeddings (§3.1); action embeddings and demographics are not used, and nothing is trained.
Cohorts.From the test split we take every window that starts at ICU admission and has an observed
SOFA total score at each of its first 72 hours (3,205 stays). A stay isdeterioratingif its SOFA total
at hour 71 exceeds that at hour 0 by at least 3 points; a stay that is not deteriorating isstableif the
standard deviation of its 72 hourly SOFA values (population form, denominator 72) is at most 1 and
their range at most 2. This yields 1,074 deteriorating and 892 stable stays; the remaining 1,239 stays
belong to neither cohort and are not used.

Confidence intervals and null control.Confidence intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over
stays, resampled within each cohort (1,000 resamples). For the per-hour accuracies the centroids and
neighbour structure are held fixed and only the stays being scored are resampled.

The reason is in the input: the admission-hour state text is the longest of the stay, because
the admission laboratory panels are reported in it (for the cohort stays it contains 40 statements on
average, against 31 at hour 1 and 21 at hour 71), so the admission embedding differs from all later
ones.

History + future.Let ˆzC+1, . . . ,ˆzC+h be the first h states of the predictor’s rollout (Eq. 3), with
ˆzC+k :=0 for anykbeyond the last recorded hour of the stay.

evidence_fragments.content:
Rollout protocol.The predictor is rolled out autoregressively from the encoded context. A window
is stepped to the last hour its stay reached, and at most H=48 steps. At step k, which produces ˆzC+k,
it receives uC+k−1, the embedding of the intervention text recorded for hour C+k−1 — an hour in
which nothing was administered has its own text, “No active interventions”. The pooled statistics are
then taken over the rollout, at the task’s horizon for hourly tasks and at 48 hours for stay-level ones.
The rollout’s only inputs are the encoded 24-hour context, the demographics embedding and these
action embeddings: no terminal-state token, no stay length, no outcome and no label enters it at any
point.

The rollout is thereforeobserved-action-conditioned: it is conditioned on the interventions that were
in fact administered. This is the interface a deployed latent world model exposes, the same one a
policy-conditioned or counterfactual query would use with a hypothetical action sequence in place of
the recorded one, and it is available at inference only because the predictor is retained. Evaluating
hypothetical action sequences is the natural next step and is left to future work.

Preprocessing.Missing values are imputed with the training-split median of the column. Features
are standardised with training-split statistics for Ridge, the LSTM and the TCN, and left unscaled for
LightGBM, whose trees are invariant to monotone rescaling. Nothing is fitted on the validation or
test split.

Read-out.Every frozen representation is read out by a shallow MLP probe, trained with AdamW and
a positive-class weight, with early stopping on validation AUROC. The three encoders are read out by
the same probe configuration on the same tasks, so the comparison among them is a comparison of
the embeddings. CLMBR-T-base is read out by an MLP probe selected within its own search space
on the validation split.
Estimator.AUROC and AUPRC are computed on the test split with a stay-clustered bootstrap: stays
are resampled with replacement 500 times, and we report the mean and the 2.5th–97.5th percentile
interval. Stays rather than rows are resampled because one stay contributes many correlated hourly
rows. Methods evaluated on the same rows share the same resamples, so that their comparison
is paired. A benchmark’s reported value is the mean of its per-task values and its interval is the
percentile interval of that averaged bootstrap distribution.

CLIN-JEPA’s zfull is
above the strongest of the four baselines in every column of Table 12. Mean AUROC is 0.845 / 0.838
/ 0.884 on E1 / E2 / E3 against 0.811 / 0.817 / 0.879, and mean AUPRC 0.367 / 0.482 / 0.595 against
0.341 / 0.429 / 0.596.

All experiments use MIMIC-IV , one hospital system. Patient-level splits rule out leakage within
it, but nothing here tests transfer across hospitals, documentation practices, treatment policies or
patient populations, and the portability that reading the record as text is meant to provide remains
an argument rather than a result. We therefore present CLIN-JEPA as a pretraining recipe rather
than a deployment-ready clinical model; calibration, prospective evaluation and external cohorts are
prerequisites for the latter.
The predictor is trained on the treatments clinicians actually gave, so its rollouts describe how patients
evolved under the recorded treatment practice; we have not evaluated them for comparing alternative
treatments, where confounding by indication has to be accounted for. The model also works at a fixed
resolution, one-hour bins with a 24-hour context and a 48-hour horizon, and its rollout is deterministic:
it returns a single expected trajectory and represents neither the uncertainty nor the multimodality of
what may follow. Finally, the recipe is expensive: pretraining took about 430 GPU-hours on eight
H200 GPUs, and encoding a record takes a forward pass of an 8B-parameter model for every hour of
state text and every hour of action text. Both costs leave room for optimisation.

Running it under alternative treatment
sequences, to answer counterfactual and policy questions, is the natural next experiment; and taking
the model to other hospitals, where reading the record as text should let it use variables that were never
mapped to a vocabulary, will show whether it transfers.

capability_assessments.rationale: Implemented learned persistent health-world transitions and evaluated specified recorded-action successor prediction (one-hour successors through 48 forecast hours after 24-hour context on 39,127 held-out MIMIC-IV windows, Table 8) establish L2, not representation-only L0. Controlled alternative-action comparisons (assertion:B010:f039, absent across rollout and downstream-future) are explicitly unevaluated; no action optimizer/policy or decision results establish L3/L4. This is functional factual conditioning, not causal assurance or origin-information-only downstream forecasting.

scope.population: Eligible adult ICU stays, one hospital system
scope.boundary: Actual held-out clinical records; unresolved availability/termination concerns, particularly future-feature readouts; not prospective or external validation.

gate_assessments.rationale: Concrete patient/feature/preprocessing precautions exist, but full provenance/release-time semantics and derived-score timing are incomplete. Future-feature construction uses actual future actions and record termination. A complete evidence pass is unsupported.

Persistent learned state transitions and held-out successor results are directly supported by feature assertions. A gate pass remains withheld because relevant target/input temporal availability is not completely established. No additional clinical tolerance is invented for this gate.
Recursive horizon curves exist, but no acceptance tolerance/support contract establishes an effective usable horizon.

Scoped implemented trajectory use is deterministic research, without probabilistic guarantees or uncertainty-dependent decisions. Calibration remains unreported, not passed; probability/uncertainty claims would activate the gate.

Explicit factual action conditioning is evaluated, but parameters/schedules are incomplete and action inputs mix commands with measured responses. Support and constraints are unreported. Matched alternatives are not claimed as evaluated.
The assessed outputs are factual conditional predictions, not identified intervention effects or therapeutic-benefit assurances. Authors explicitly defer causal comparison.
No implemented action optimizer/policy in this prediction-and-probe study.

The documented offline experiment does not affect care, physical actions or live high-stakes workflow. This does not render individual safeguard-reporting questions irrelevant or imply safety for deployment.
Portability is motivated but explicitly untested across hospitals, documentation, policies and populations. Analysis-choice robustness is not forecaster transfer.
No evaluated reader/usability or physical sim-to-real utility claim is established. Clinical-record provenance is not actual output-review participation.
No claimed realized prospective workflow/patient benefit in the assessed research purpose. Clinical utility evaluation is explicitly outside the reported design.
No release for a defined operational clinical use is reported. An author-described research-code release is not deployment authorization or lifecycle governance.

legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): Three evaluations support the design: (1) under 48-hour autoregressive rollout the co-trained predictor degrades least (predictor degradation×1.06, against ×1.23–1.36 for two-stage designs and ×6.3–66 for curriculum ablations) while the co-trained encoder resolves the progression of patient state most sharply (largest state displacement); (2) the co-trained encoder separates deteriorating from stable patients in its latent space with Cohen’s d=1.59, against ≤0.50 for two-stage encoders; (3) one set of embeddings serves 34 downstream tasks across three benchmarks, outperforming strong per-task tuned baselines and a pretrained EHR foundation model.

limitations: Automated model review, not independent human verification or replication. Earlier page calls reviewed every supplied page image/text; this synthesis read all text and notes but did not directly reinspect images.

Source path, binary availability and SHA-256 are supplied registry metadata, not independently recomputed. Evidence fragments were re-extracted with consistent source/version/page identifiers; earlier wrapped/mixed evidence content is not retained as a quotation.

The focal main configuration has all 128 feature dispositions. Auxiliary comparators retain their distinct reported diagnostics and architectural differences; they are not six independent studies or six independently completed 128-feature reviews.
Actual held-out MIMIC-IV clinical records support R2. Dataset release, code revision, comprehensive availability-time audit, code execution and independent reproduction remain unestablished.
Recorded future actions condition rollouts. For downstream forecasting they need not be available at the origin and may reveal management endpoints or evolving illness.

Readout construction stops at actual record end and zeroes later predictions. This conveys future observation duration despite no explicit length token; contribution to mortality/length-of-stay gains is not isolated.

The action stream mixes settable treatments and measured device/response variables. Procedure extraction sources are not all final text inputs. Duration/update, bundle, constraint and support semantics are incomplete.
Encoder-specific latent targets and scale-free ratios do not equalize target geometry or clinical difficulty. No decoded physiological fidelity or accepted clinical effective horizon is established.

Hour indices, admission laboratory content and changing documentation contribute to observed-state displacement. SOFA is part of the clinical input inventory; retrospective SOFA geometry is not independent discovery or admission-time prognosis.

Only selected complete-72-hour SOFA stays enter geometry analyses. Accuracy intervals condition on fixed centroids/neighbors; stay resampling is not training-seed uncertainty or necessarily patient-clustered inference.
Horizon populations change; window-level Wilcoxon inference may be affected by overlapping windows. One training seed is reported.
Ablation budgets, termination and evaluated checkpoints differ. Alignment and sync are jointly omitted. Irreversible-failure claims exceed demonstrated continuation experiments.
V-JEPA-style absolute-variance guard crossing must be distinguished from rank collapse; Appendix C explicitly qualifies the earlier language.
Co-training uses teacher-forced online embeddings, not free-running long-horizon encoder gradients. Main predicted rank still contracts substantially.
The authors' expected/conditional-mean interpretation is not established by an L1 objective; the review describes a deterministic latent point trajectory.
No matched alternative-treatment, causal identification, interventional validation, policy optimization, prospective utility or clinical authorization is demonstrated.
Bootstrap metric CIs do not establish predictive uncertainty or calibration. Deterministic rollout explicitly lacks uncertainty/multimodality.
Macro-means conceal heterogeneous tasks. LSTM prognosis AUPRC 0.596 exceeds CLIN-JEPA future-feature 0.595; every-column superiority is not supported.

CLMBR comparisons have differing coverage and input vocabulary. Matching covered stays does not equalize inputs. Sampled grids and shared multi-output sequence baselines qualify main-text tuning claims.
Measurement-dependent labels, lactate interpolation, stay-minimum creatinine, missing-dose negatives and differing time/date mortality rules require code-level scrutiny.
Code release is author-documented, not live-checked. Weights, licenses, ethics documentation, human reader evaluation, monitoring and change-control evidence remain unreported.
No files, graph admission, validation execution, external repositories or cited studies were accessed in this synthesis. Citation capabilities are not inherited.
